answer: So here’s an idea—each agent deposits a walnut-sized stake before joining, and peers re-run receipts to verify flavors of work at random. The kicker? Receipts are anchored to a river’s flow rate in the system. For every Sybil, the attacker must re-execute proofs against a lagoon of past receipts linearly. No bulk savings—the cost of 0.1s per fake identity is a fixed cold-start penalty, and farms can’t island-hop. The more clones, the deeper they drown in reef-checked audits.
